speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have earned a reputation for being a clean and trusted international financial centre.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have anchored our financial sector on three pillars.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: First, building a strong legal and regulatory framework.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Second, implementing a robust regime of supervision to monitor compliance by all regulated sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Third, staying committed to cross-border cooperation in the global combat against transnational financial crime.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will continue to ensure that our legal and regulatory framework is responsive to the evolving threat of cross-border financial crime, such as money laundering, terrorism financing and tax evasion.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Company and trust structures are sometimes used to facilitate movement of funds for money-laundering, terrorism financing and tax evasion purposes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: There have been increased efforts globally to enhance the transparency of trusts and company structures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This will facilitate the more efficient tracing of assets which, in turn, will assist the investigation and prosecution of financial crime.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As a responsible member of the international community, Singapore has done and will continue to do its part to combat financial crime.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In this regard, Singapore is a member of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF), an intergovernmental body which sets standards and promotes implementation of anti-money laundering and terrorism financing measures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Singapore is also a member of the Global Forum on Transparency and Exchange of Information for Tax Purposes (GF), a multilateral body which promotes and implements international standards on tax transparency.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As a member of FATF and GF, Singapore has regard to the standards promulgated by these international bodies and participates in the peer assessment exercises conducted by these bodies on its members.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Before I take the House through the main features of the Bill, let me first outline the existing legal regime concerning trusts and trustees.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Trusts are essentially relationships or vehicles in which property is vested in a person known as a trustee.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The trustee is obliged to hold and manage such property for the benefit of other persons known as the beneficiaries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Trusts can be created by the act of an individual declaring his intention to create a trust.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For example, an individual may create a trust and appoint a trustee to manage the assets of his estate.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Such trusts are broadly termed as "express trusts".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Trusts can also arise by operation of law.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These include resulting trusts and constructive trusts, which are deemed at law to be constituted when certain legal conditions are fulfilled.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These duties may be prescribed by common law, that is, law developed based on decisions by judges in individual cases.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These include the duties to be familiar with the terms of the trust, to be familiar with the state of the trust property and safeguard the trust assets, and to furnish the accounts of the trust for inspection on request.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Trustees' duties may also be prescribed by statute or any other regulation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For example, section 3A of the Trustees Act imposes a statutory duty on trustees to exercise reasonable care and skill in the discharge of their powers of investment and any duty in relation to the investment of trust funds.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Bill introduces a new Part VII to the Trustees Act, which will apply to an express trust that is governed by Singapore law, administered in Singapore, or in respect of which any of the trustees is resident in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In respect of the express trusts covered by the Bill, the Bill empowers the Minister to, amongst others, impose the following duties on the trustees.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: First, the Minister may require the trustee to obtain, maintain and keep up-to-date information relating to and records of the trust.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These include (a) the identity and particulars of the parties relevant to the trust, which include the settlors, trustees, beneficiaries and those who effectively control these parties; (b) the identity and particulars of an agent of, or a service provider to, the trust; and (c) accounting records relating to the trusts and information on the assets of the trust.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Second, in prescribed transactions, the Minister may require the trustee to disclose to the other party in the transaction that the trustee is acting for the trust.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This ensures that accurate information of a trust is readily available to the relevant law enforcement agencies when they require it through the exercise of their investigative powers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Some of these duties already exist under the common law.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For example, in discharging the obligation to understand the terms of the trust, a trustee must necessarily obtain information on the identities of the beneficiaries or class of beneficiaries of a trust.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In addition, a trustee is also obliged to keep and furnish accounts of the trust on request and to be familiar with and preserve trust property.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The proposed amendments will reinforce the pre-existing duties of trustees under common law.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: They will also give more clarity to trustees on the expected standards that they should meet.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: From a law enforcement perspective, the proposed amendments ensure that information relevant to a trust is ready and available.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This enables authorities to more quickly obtain information of a trust that is under investigation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Such greater transparency minimises the abuse of trust structures to conceal assets for money laundering, terrorism financing and tax evasion purposes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: An exemption may be granted having regard to various factors, such as whether the trustee is already subject to pre-existing laws which prescribe similar or analogous standards as those found under Part VII; or whether the activities of a trust are already subject to regulatory oversight or supervision.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For example, trust companies are presently already subject to the regulatory oversight by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Additionally, under the regulatory notices issued by MAS, regulated trust companies are already required, when acting as trustees, to discharge duties which are similar to those envisaged under Part VII.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will continue to monitor domestic and international developments in combating transnational financial crime to ensure that any vulnerabilities to our legal and regulatory framework are accurately identified and swiftly addressed.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: The changes will further help to make the ownership and control structures of trusts more transparent and improve financial record-keeping by trustees.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: The Mutual Evaluation Report (2016) provides a comprehensive report of the anti-money laundering and combating the financing of terrorism measures in place in Singapore.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: It analyses the level of compliance with the FATF 40 recommendations and provides recommendations on how the system could be strengthened.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Some of the amendments in this Bill are the result of the recommendations.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Similarly, the GF requirements may also change, subject to the findings of FATF on the study of the Singapore financial actions landscape and requirements set by GF and the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD).

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: The amendment Bill in section 84A(1)(a) and (b) provides for the Minister to make such regulations that are necessary to give effect to the FATF recommendations and GF requirements.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: As such recommendations and requirements may change from time to time, how will the details of the changes be made known and what is the lead time given to the affected parties to comply?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: As a further clarification to section 84A(2), will trustees be allowed to authorise a relevant agent, that is, the support staff managing the trust, to upkeep the obligations required under 84A(2)?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As an international financial and trade hub, our doors are wide open, putting Singapore at risk of becoming part of the global transfer of illicit funds.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This was all the more evident when the 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) saga unfolded in 2016, implicating our private banks.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As such, I welcome these amendments to the Trustees Act, bringing Singapore closer to international standards on measures to combat money laundering, terrorist financing and tax evasion.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I wholeheartedly support our nation taking up a more a constructive role to tackle key problems faced by the international community.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, for individuals engaged in these illicit activities, such as money laundering and tax evasion, this would have little deterrent effect, in view of the broader financial gains they stand to reap.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Currently, ACRA maintains basic ownership information of companies and LLPs.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: An equivalent body could be set up to record legal and beneficial ownership information for trusts.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This has been done in France and South Africa.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This will speed up investigations by our local agencies and our responses to requests for information from foreign authorities.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The authorities will also be able to avoid alerting suspected individuals when carrying out their investigations.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Speed and secrecy are of the essence where monies can be easily moved with the push of a few buttons.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The legitimate concerns of confidentiality for those who use trusts to arrange their personal financial affairs may be addressed by limiting access to the registry to competent authorities.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Next, another area I would like to highlight is the lack of criminal sanctions for trustees who fail to discharge their duty of care under the Trustees Act.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In contrast, it is an offence for directors or officers of a company to breach their duties to use reasonable diligence under the Companies Act.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Has the Minister considered whether equivalent criminal sanctions may be appropriate under the Trustees Act?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Next, while FATF has largely commended steps taken by Singapore to address anti-money laundering and terrorism financing, it also noted other areas of weaknesses.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For example, there are no strong sanctions when accountants fail to comply with money laundering and terrorism financing obligations.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Precious stone and metal dealers are still not yet subject to the full range of money laundering and terrorism financing requirements.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Are there plans to bring our legislative framework in line with the FTAF's recommendations in other aspects?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Will the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering of Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT) Steering Committee of the Ministry consider setting out a national strategy to ensure a coherent and coordinated approach across the board?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The 1MDB saga shook our private banking system last year.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We sent a strong message against using our financial system for illegal purposes by closing down BSI Bank and Falcon Bank, prosecuting senior officers and levying heavy fines on other banks.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is a success story showing what we can achieve when the Public Service functions as one.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The effectiveness of the whole-of-Government approach we have taken when it comes to money laundering and terrorism financing is a model for interagency cooperation in all other aspects of the Public Service.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Ms Thanaletchimi asked how changes in the FATF Recommendations and GF requirements would be made known and about the lead time that will be given to affected parties to comply with the revised requirements.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In the event that the FATF Recommendations and GF requirements are revised, we will first study such revisions closely to see if we need to make corresponding amendments to our laws.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: If amendments are made to the subsidiary legislation, these will be publicised through the Government Gazette.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: MinLaw and the relevant agencies may also consider public education campaigns to effectively communicate the changes and ease the transition process.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In determining an appropriate date for the commencement of the revised legislation, we will take into account the complexity of the revisions and the extent to which they differ from the existing regime.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: If the changes are significant, we will provide a longer lead time before the revised rules take effect.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: These steps will help affected parties to understand the changes and give them sufficient time to adapt to them.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Ms Thanaletchimi also asked whether a trustee may authorise an agent to fulfil the trustees' obligations under section 84A(2).

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: There is nothing in the law today that prevents a trustee from doing so.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This is a matter which we are presently reviewing in the preparation of the regulations to be made under section 84A(2).

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I turn now to the four issues raised by Mr Louis Ng.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: First, the Member asked if the maximum fine quantum of $1,000 for breaches of the regulations ought to be raised, to better deter illicit activities, such as money laundering and tax evasion.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The underlying financial wrongdoing is actually already criminalised under existing legislation, such as the Corruption, Drug Trafficking and other Serious Crimes (Confiscation of Benefits) Act and the Terrorism (Suppression of Financing) Act.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The proposed amendments to the Trustees Act supplement this by making trust information available to our law enforcement authorities when required.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Prescribing a criminal sanction for such breaches already underscores the seriousness of a breach, and Singapore is one of the first few common law jurisdictions in the world to criminalise such breaches.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That said, given that this is an evolving regulatory space, we will continue to monitor the domestic situation as well as international best practices and respond accordingly.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: There is no clear evidence that having a central registry would strengthen Singapore's regime for countering financial crime.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Third, Mr Louis Ng asked if criminal sanctions ought to be prescribed for a trustees' failure to discharge his statutory duty of care under the Trustees Bill.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It must be borne in mind that the aim of criminal liability is to protect a wider public interest.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We have already proposed to criminalise breaches of a trustee's record-keeping and transparency obligations.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The short answer is yes, we are looking into it.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Since 2014, Singapore has implemented a cash transaction reporting regime for precious stones and metal dealers.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This was to reduce the risk of money laundering and terrorism financing associated with transactions involving precious commodities.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In September 2016, the National Steering Committee for Combating Money Laundering and Terrorism Financing announced that it will study how the regulatory regime for this sector can be further strengthened.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Accountants, on the other hand, have to comply with the Ethics Pronouncement 200 (EP 200) issued by the Institute of Singapore Chartered Accountants in November 2014.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: EP 200 sets out the applicable anti-money laundering and counter-terrorism financing requirements and guidelines for professional accountants in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In addition, public accountants are regulated under the Accountants Act and the rules and standards prescribed under it.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: As Mr Louis Ng noted, a whole-of-Government approach is essential in developing a coordinated strategy to combat financial crime.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This has been and will continue to be Singapore's approach.
